reference_status: Owner supplied Utilities menu with Export Items selected. Detailed export-screen layout, columns and reference output file have not been supplied; visual/file-format equivalence is not certified.

findings.current_behavior: CSV quoting doubles quotes but does not neutralize formula-like text. The actual CSV encoder emitted a synthetic customer name =1+1 unchanged as a cell. Spreadsheet applications may interpret such values as formulas depending on how the file is opened/imported.
findings.required_correction: Apply a documented spreadsheet-safe CSV text policy to untrusted fields, covering leading formula characters and control/whitespace variants while preserving legitimate numeric values. Keep XLSX values explicit strings and test both formats.
findings.evidence: Actual encoder/parser probe returned =1+1 unchanged. No spreadsheet or formula was executed. The XLSX counterpart was verified as ExcelJS ValueType.String, not a formula object. Source exports.ts:9–16.

findings.classification: Silent export truncation and unstable ordering
findings.current_behavior: Every dataset query takes at most 10,000 rows without orderBy or continuation. The response has only bytes/contentType and the UI provides no total, truncation message or continuation. A 10,001-row mock honoring the actual take argument yielded 10,000 output records.
findings.required_correction: Export all authorized rows using stable ordering and bounded streaming/chunks, or disclose the limit and provide a complete authorized continuation mechanism. Add a greater-than-limit completeness test.
findings.evidence: Synthetic query-cap probe and actual CSV output; no real large database was queried. Source exports.ts:54/68/82/103/117 and page.tsx.

findings.current_behavior: Exported Customers omit branch; Items omit unit/category; Projects omit customer/branch. Passing the actual generated CSV into actual import preview rejects the files with missing-column errors. Empty CSV has zero bytes and empty XLSX uses no_data rather than dataset headers. The screen does not explain these schema limitations.
findings.required_correction: Define whether exports are analytical or import-ready. For import-ready exports, provide scoped relational references and shared column schemas; otherwise clearly label limitations and offer an explicit import-ready format. Keep headers for empty datasets.
findings.evidence: Actual CSV→parse/preview probes: Customers MISSING_COLUMNS:branch; Items MISSING_COLUMNS:unit,category; Projects MISSING_COLUMNS:customer,branch. Empty CSV probe produced zero bytes. Source exports.ts and imports.ts requiredHeaders.
findings.policy_note: The screen never explicitly promises round-trip restore. The finding is a concrete portability/documentation gap, not proof that the existing UI made that promise.

findings.classification: Inventory/item feature policy inconsistent across entry points
findings.current_behavior: The selected Export Items navigation entry requires INVENTORY and enabled item features, but the generic Export page always includes Items. The export endpoint requires ACCOUNT_REPORTS only and does not consult Inventory/item-feature state. A synthetic authorized direct item export returned data without reading disabled-module configuration.
findings.required_correction: Apply one explicit feature policy to menu, generic page and Web/mobile export endpoints. If read-only exports must remain available after Inventory is disabled, document that deliberate exception and make the entry points consistent rather than silently expanding operational permissions.
findings.evidence: Source navigation.ts Export Items requiredModules/requiresItems; actual exportAccountData wrapper probe used ACCOUNT_REPORTS and never called the disabled-module provider. No unauthorized production export or cross-company access is asserted.

findings.current_behavior: An unsupported format is rejected only after the dataset query and row transformation. The Web route does not translate unsupported type/format into a documented 400 response; mobile uses the generic unexpected-error path.
findings.required_correction: Validate the type/format allowlists before reading business rows and map invalid requests to consistent safe 400 responses with no data query.
findings.evidence: Actual unsupported-format probe queried customers once then threw UNSUPPORTED_EXPORT_FORMAT. Web/mobile status behavior is source inference, not live HTTP execution.

findings.current_behavior: The Android share handler uses the XLSX MIME type only for .xlsx and application/json for every other file. Generated .csv exports are therefore shared as JSON, which can affect available apps and interpretation.
findings.required_correction: Carry the actual authorized download MIME type through the native file-delivery DTO, or use a validated extension-to-MIME mapping including text/csv. Verify Android share targets and receiving-app behavior for CSV, XLSX and JSON backup.
findings.evidence: Source AccountUtilityScreen.kt:124–131. Physical chooser/receiving-app behavior not tested.
